newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania parliament rejects motion on farm policies.
newsitem.headline: Romania parliament rejects motion on farm policies.

text.p: Romania's parliament rejected on Thursday an opposition motion accusing the new centrist government of mishandling agrarian policies.
The motion, launched by the leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), was rejected by 176 votes to 125, parliament officials said.
The former ruling PDSR had accused Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's government of "incompetence in solving the disastrous situation" in the farming sector.
"This government lacks a coherent policy in agriculture," PDSR executive president Adrian Nastase told parliament.
The PDSR cited delays in starting spring farm works and equipment repairs, cuts in import taxes for food produce, high prices for fertilisers, seeds and fuel as reasons for launching the motion.
During the debate, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu defended the cabinet's policy and rejected the motion as groundless.
"It is impossible for us to repair in three months what was destroyed by those who had the power for seven years," he said in a reference to previous leftist governments' policies.
Ciorbea's coalition cabinet relies on a comfortable majority in the parliament, dominated by centrists who ended the ex-communists' seven-year grip on power in last year's elections.

Two weeks ago the government announced radical reforms, including fast privatisation and restructuring of communist-era loss-making plants, including pig and poultry farms, subsidy cuts and price liberalisation.
The PDSR, ousted in elections last November, had stalled reform of the farming sector, clinging to communist-era farm policies and subsidies for agriculture, mainly for electoral purposes.
